proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §5 (the cubical grid and its faces F ∈ 𝓛_n, of Hⁿ-measure 1, used throughout the proof of 5.1), as stated in step 1(a), (c), (d) of the parent proof (φ_p is an isometric embedding with φ_p([0,1]ⁿ) = F_p and φ_p((0,1)ⁿ) = F_p°; μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; diam F_p ≤ √P; F_p is closed; distinct open faces avoid the other closed faces). Notation as in the statement; since ι is strictly increasing it is injective, so n ≤ P. ê_k is the k-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ.

1. Coordinates of Φ_p. The i-th coordinate of e_{ι(j)} is 1 if i = ι(j) and 0 otherwise, and ι is injective; hence (Φ_p y)_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + y_k for every k < n and (Φ_p y)_i = z_i for every i ∉ range ι.

2. (6), and Φ_p is a measurable embedding. By step 1, Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y') has coordinate y_k − y'_k at ι(k) and 0 at every i ∉ range ι, so ‖Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y')‖² = Σ_k (y_k − y'_k)² = ‖y − y'‖², i.e. dist(Φ_p(y), Φ_p(y')) = dist(y, y'). Thus Φ_p is an isometry ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (Lipschitz with constant 1, continuous, injective); an isometry from a complete space has closed range and is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding).

3. (5) and F_p = Φ_p(C), C := [0,1]ⁿ. If 0 ≤ y_k ≤ 1 for all k, step 1 gives (Φ_p y)_{ι(k)} ∈ [z_{ι(k)}, z_{ι(k)} + 1] and (Φ_p y)_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι, so Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p: this is (5). Conversely, for x ∈ F_p put y_k := x_{ι(k)} − z_{ι(k)} ∈ [0,1]; by step 1, Φ_p(y) and x have the same coordinates, so x = Φ_p(y). Hence F_p = Φ_p(C) and, Φ_p being injective, Φ_p⁻¹(F_p) = C.

4. (1), and Q₁ = C almost everywhere. The coordinate map ℝⁿ = Euclid n → (Fin n → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, equivalently EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp); it maps Q₁ onto the box ∏_k (0,1) and C onto ∏_k [0,1]. By volume_pi_Ioo and volume_Icc_pi both boxes have volume ∏_k ofReal(1 − 0) = 1. So volume(Q₁) = 1 = volume(C) < ∞, and as Q₁ ⊆ C, volume(C ∖ Q₁) = 0, i.e. volume⌞C = volume⌞Q₁ (equivalently Measure.univ_pi_Ioo_ae_eq_Icc).

5. (8). F_p = ⋂_{i<P} S_i with S_i := {x : (i ∈ range ι → z_i ≤ x_i ∧ x_i ≤ z_i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ range ι → x_i = z_i)}. For fixed i exactly one of the two implications is non-vacuous, so S_i is {x : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1} or {x : x_i = z_i}, the preimage of a closed subset of ℝ under the continuous coordinate map x ↦ x_i. So every S_i, and hence F_p, is closed; in particular F_p is Borel.

6. (3). On Euclid n, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Since Φ_p is an isometry, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives Φ_p#(volume) = Φ_p#(μHE[n]) = μHE[n]⌞(range Φ_p). Restrict both sides to the Borel set F_p ⊆ range Φ_p (step 3). On the left, by MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and step 3, (Φ_p#volume)⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Φ_p⁻¹(F_p)) = Φ_p#(volume⌞C) = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁) (step 4). On the right, (μHE[n]⌞range Φ_p)⌞F_p = μHE[n]⌞(F_p ∩ range Φ_p) = μHE[n]⌞F_p (Measure.restrict_restrict, F_p Borel). Hence μHE[n]⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁).

7. (2). Evaluating (3) on ℝ^P: Hⁿ(F_p) = (μHE[n]⌞F_p)(ℝ^P) = (Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁))(ℝ^P) = volume(Q₁) = 1 by (1).

8. (4). Because Φ_p is a measurable embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives ∫ f d(Φ_p#ν) = ∫ (f∘Φ_p) dν for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, integrable or not. With ν := volume⌞Q₁ and (3): ∫_{F_p} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f(Φ_p(y)) dy.

9. (7). Let x, x' ∈ F_p. For i ∉ range ι, x_i = z_i = x'_i; for i ∈ range ι, x_i, x'_i ∈ [z_i, z_i + 1], so |x_i − x'_i| ≤ 1. Hence dist(x, x')² = Σ_{i ∈ range ι} (x_i − x'_i)² ≤ #(range ι) = n ≤ P and dist(x, x') ≤ √P.

10. (9). Let q = (z', ι') with ι' strictly increasing, y ∈ Q₁ and x := Φ_p(y), and suppose x ∈ F_q. By step 1, for k < n, x_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + y_k with 0 < y_k < 1, so x_{ι(k)} ∉ ℤ. As x ∈ F_q, x_i = z'_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∉ range ι'. Hence every ι(k) lies in range ι', i.e. range ι ⊆ range ι'. Both ranges have exactly n elements (ι, ι' injective on Fin n), so range ι = range ι'; two strictly increasing maps Fin n → Fin P with the same range coincide (each is the increasing enumeration of that set: Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique, or StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so ι' = ι. For i ∉ range ι, z'_i = x_i = z_i (x ∈ F_q and step 1). For i = ι(k), z_i < x_i < z_i + 1 and z'_i ≤ x_i ≤ z'_i + 1 with z_i, z'_i ∈ ℤ: z'_i ≥ z_i + 1 would give x_i ≥ z_i + 1, and z'_i ≤ z_i − 1 would give x_i ≤ z_i, both impossible; so z'_i = z_i. Thus z' = z and ι' = ι, i.e. q = p. Consequently, if q ≠ p then Φ_p(y) ∉ F_q. ∎
key_steps: Coordinates: (Φ_p y)_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + y_k and (Φ_p y)_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι (ι injective).
Φ_p is an isometry, hence a closed and measurable embedding, and F_p = Φ_p([0,1]ⁿ).
volume(Q₁) = volume([0,1]ⁿ) = 1 through the measure-preserving coordinate identification; the cube boundary is null.
Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure with μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ gives Hⁿ⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁); hence Hⁿ(F_p) = 1 and ∫_{F_p} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f∘Φ_p for all f.
Coordinate estimates give diam F_p ≤ √n ≤ √P and closedness of F_p.
The non-integer coordinates of a point of Φ_p(Q₁) determine ι and z, so Φ_p(Q₁) ∩ F_q = ∅ for q ≠ p.
